population.note: FICTIONAL. There are about 276M adults. Current users are 36.8% (≈101.6M) and ever-users are 49.0% (≈135.2M). Ever-use rose 9.0 pts, inside the 11.3-pt limit. Cycling arithmetic: ever 49.0 − current 36.8 = 12.2 pts off now (≈33.7M). About 18.0 pts of current users are on a second or later course, and about 5.5 pts of the off-now group restarted and then stopped again, so (18.0 + 5.5)/49.0 ≈ 48% have cycled. That is consistent with ~35% one-year persistence and 36–47% restart within a year. Employer retreat added forced stops: about 3M commercial users lost weight-management coverage in 2035. Most restarted on cash orals, on imports or in the federal community programme, and that restarting is what keeps the cycling share high. Age check: 18–29: 22% × 52M = 11.4M; 30–49: 41% × 92M = 37.7M; 50–64: 51% × 62M = 31.6M; 65+: 30% × 70M = 21.0M. Total ≈ 101.7M ≈ 36.8%. Under-30 growth is driven mostly by vaping-cessation and drinking-reduction use, not weight. Income thirds average (40 + 35 + 35.4)/3 = 36.8. The middle third is now the lowest. It lost employer coverage and earns too much for the free community programme, so its growth is mostly cash orals and imports. The bottom third rose because of ≈6.0M free-programme users plus Medicaid and imports. About 10.5M of the 21.0M users aged 65+ have used for more than 2 years. Never-users (≈141M, 51%) skew to rural over-65s, people with contraindications, refusers by conviction, and young adults without a nicotine or drinking indication. Pediatric use: 1.4% × 73M ≈ 1.0M, mostly adolescents 12+. Roughly one child in two now lives with a parent who is on the drug or cycling off it.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. Part D obesity benefit unchanged: $199/month statutory rate, $50 copay, counselling visit, BMI ≥30 or ≥27 with one comorbidity. Retatrutide 12 mg was added to formularies at the statutory rate in Apr 2035. Medicare pays 20.3% of fills, ≈20.6M users (≈19.0M aged 65+, ≈1.6M disabled): ≈9.0M for diabetes and ≈11.6M for obesity. Obesity-benefit spend: 11.6M × $199 × 12 ≈ $27.7B gross; copays 11.6M × $50 × 12 ≈ $7.0B; net to programme ≈$20.7B. All Medicare incretin fills: 20.6M × $199 × 12 ≈ $49.2B gross. Medicaid: the same 31 states plus DC at the 90% match. It pays 12.8% of fills, ≈13.0M × $199 × 12 ≈ $31.0B gross. NEW: the Community Metabolic Access Program (HRSA, enacted Jul 2035) buys oral semaglutide (incl. 50 mg) and Foundayo at a federal volume price of $99/month. It supplies them free through FQHCs to uninsured and underinsured adults at or below 200% FPL, in all states including non-expansion states, and through state tobacco quitlines and SAMHSA-funded alcohol programmes. It reaches ≈6.0M users (≈4.4M metabolic, ≈1.6M nicotine/alcohol): 6.0M × $99 × 12 ≈ $7.1B a year, against a $7.5B annual appropriation.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 100+ semaglutide brands at $4–25/month and generic oral semaglutide; first oral 'tirzepatide-like' copies are sold domestically. China: generic semaglutide and tirzepatide, plus 'research' retatrutide vials and powder sold openly on export platforms. Canada: generic semaglutide at CAD 40–70. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Egypt all have generics. US: the mid-2035 contingent date for rival generic semaglutide filers did not trigger. The first filer contested FDA's forfeiture determination of its 180-day exclusivity in D.D.C., and the rivals' settlement dates are tied to that forfeiture. A ruling is expected 2037.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Prices stepped down through managed channels. An HHS–manufacturer portal agreement (Apr 2035) set these direct prices: injectable semaglutide and tirzepatide $199–249; Wegovy pill 50 mg $229; oral starters still $149–150; retatrutide 12 mg $299 (list cut from $1,649 to $1,449); amycretin $399; MariTide $449. PBM net is ≈$170–185. Payer mix of ≈101.6M users: commercial 25.6% (26.0M, of which ≈15M are under diabetes, cardiac, OSA, MASH or CKD codes and only ≈11M under weight management); Medicare 20.3% (20.6M); Medicaid 12.8% (13.0M); federal community programme 5.9% (6.0M); cash/direct 24.6% (25.0M, including ≈5.5M 'calm' and 'focus' subscribers and ≈1.8M telehealth nicotine/alcohol patients); imported/counterfeit 10.8% (11.0M). Sum = 101.6M = 100%. Of the 49% of employers still covering weight management, ~90% gate it. Routes: ≈44% oral, ≈52% weekly injectable, ≈4% monthly. The 503B exclusion and 503A injunction stand.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic, incl. 7.2 mg)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg single-dose autoinjector on the portal and Part D from 2035)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GIPR-antagonist/GLP-1 agonist antibody-peptide conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill incl. 50 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol use disorder: guideline-endorsed second-line (ASAM and VA/DoD, Oct 2035), sNDA under FDA review; ≈2.4M users

smoking and vaping cessation: endorsed in the 2035 Public Health Service tobacco guideline update as an adjunct for smokers with obesity or prior failed quits; dispensed free via state quitlines; ≈2.0M users
'metabolic health' / longevity regimens in concierge practices
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
gray-market 'research' retatrutide among gym and physique users, now partly displaced by the $299 portal pen
gambling and compulsive-shopping craving reduction, still anecdotal
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. triple_agonist_30pct is honoured by an existing product in a new form and channel, not a new molecule. In Apr 2035 Lilly's retatrutide 12 mg (~28–30% mean loss) launched as a single-dose autoinjector on the HHS portal at $299 and went onto Part D at the statutory rate, which put surgical-grade loss in a mass-market pen. Bariatric surgery volume fell ~20% in 2035. No new triple agonist is approved in the US. A Chinese triple agonist launched in China in 2036 and is not filed in the US. Survodutide's MASH sNDA was approved Aug 2035. Nicotine and alcohol: no FDA approval this step. The semaglutide AUD sNDA was filed Feb 2036 on a 52-week NIAAA-cofunded RCT, with a decision no earlier than Feb 2037. The SHAPS smoking trial completed enrolment and reads out in 2037. Guideline endorsement realises the driver. Bimagrumab + semaglutide was filed Jun 2036, with approval no earlier than mid-2037. Lilly next-generation orals remain in development and are not on the market. Incretin market: US ≈$196B = ≈90.6M paying users (101.6M − 11.0M imports) × ≈$180 average net × 12. Ex-US ≈$22B and eroding. Volume up, unit price down.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Most common effect and the leading cause of stops. Retatrutide's move to mass market raised absolute GI-related ED visits.
Rising with high-dose regimens and a 65+ user base of 21M.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Now the second-largest claim category in the consolidated MDL. Counterfeit and overdosed product heavily confound reports.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled. Mass tort: see the gastroparesis/obstruction entry.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈2.3M long-term older users meet sarcopenia criteria in Medicare claims. Retatrutide on Part D raises the lean-mass share of loss among untrained over-65s.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label; body-composition monitoring in high-efficacy labels; CMS annual DEXA requirement unchanged.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈10.5M users aged 65+ have more than 2 years' use. 10.5M × ~0.6%/yr × 0.35 excess ≈ 22,000 excess hip fractures a year, against ~310,000 US total. DEXA waits are 8–14 weeks.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelling retained; bone endpoints required; CMS 90-day bone-pause code unchanged. DOJ civil case against Novo still unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: RR ≈1.7. 101.6M users × ~4/100,000 × 0.7 ≈ 2,800 excess cases a year, mostly partial and permanent loss in one eye.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings and Precautions since May 2034; not boxed; NAION claims join the MDL.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, 'the grey')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: First randomised measurement: the 2035 AUD trial found clinically meaningful SHAPS elevation in ~9% on semaglutide 2.4 mg versus ~4% on placebo at 52 weeks. Observational 12 mg retatrutide data (~12% vs 5%) stand. Low-dose 'calm' use is still unmeasured in an RCT.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA requested anhedonia monitoring in the AUD sNDA review; no label change yet. FTC consent orders stand.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About 3M forced stops from the 2035 employer retreat, plus gating, bone-pause and holiday-related lapses.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CMS bone-pause code; Seventh Circuit still silent on the Indiana waiver.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Common in high-loss older users, retatrutide users without coaching, and import users with no clinical contact.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; the FQHC programme adds a mandatory baseline labs panel.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~10 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of follow-up. The adolescent bone readout (2035) showed a modest accrual deficit, ~0.2 SD at 2 years, with clinical meaning disputed. Cycling still looks worse for bone than continuous use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Adolescent labels updated to recommend baseline DEXA; postmarketing requirements continue.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Import and counterfeit users rose from 7.1M to ≈11.0M. Vial infections continue at a lower rate as the $299 retatrutide pen undercuts 'research' vials. Poison-centre calls are up a further ~40% on 2034.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: More import alerts (nine exporters); CDC advisories; Safe Pens bill stalled; individuals not prosecuted.

safety_ledger.effect: Counterfeit oral tablets (variable content and adulteration)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded. A Jun 2035 cluster of pressed 'Wegovy pill' tablets adulterated with glibenclamide caused ≈1,900 ED visits for severe hypoglycaemia and 23 deaths in Texas, Arizona and New Mexico.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA and CDC warnings; DEA–CBP parcel task force; NABP verified-pharmacy list; no authentication law.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent; absolute numbers up with the mass launch.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fall-related ED visits remain elevated in long-term 65+ users, especially new retatrutide starters over 70.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening mandatory in the Part D counselling visit.

safety_ledger.effect: Adverse body-composition cycling (fat-dominant regain after lean-dominant loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Concentrated in middle-third workers cut off in 2035 and in weekend 'holiday' users of the short-half-life oral.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Joint society guidance published 2035 discouraging stop-start use; no regulatory action.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Several bpm at 12 mg retatrutide; CV outcomes trial still ongoing.

safety_ledger.effect: Persistent gastroparesis, ileus and bowel obstruction (mass-tort scale)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Ileus is labelled. Persistence after stopping is unproven. The consolidated federal MDL in E.D. Pa. plus state dockets passed ≈92,000 claims (gastroparesis, obstruction, pancreatitis and now NAION). Plaintiff advertising fills daytime TV.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: First bellwether (Mar 2036): $11.2M plaintiff verdict on failure-to-warn for pre-2023 gastroparesis risk, under appeal. Novo and Lilly disclose litigation reserves; no FDA label change beyond existing ileus language.

food_and_beverage.state: With 36.8% of adults on the drug, salty-snack volume falls ~5% a year and confectionery ~6%. Two PE candy portfolios restructured. Protein and fortified dairy lead. The 'regain value pack' tier grows in middle-income suburbs hit by employer retreat. The free FQHC programme feeds a SNAP-eligible 'protein box' push from discount grocers.

alcohol.state: Ninth straight year of spirits decline, accelerated by the AUD guideline and EAP referrals. Beer volume down ~4% a year. Bar closures cluster in college towns and Milwaukee neighbourhood taverns. Non-alcoholic is now ~6% of beer volume. Tobacco and vape sales fall fastest on record as quitlines dispense free pills.

restaurants.state: Traffic flat, spend per cover down ~13% from 2028. Gram-priced bowls are universal. In Charlotte, SouthPark rooms serve 'coached' tasting portions while east Charlotte buffets and wing bars pick up the cycling-off crowd.

apparel.state: The structured/cycle split is now industry standard. 'Retatrutide fit' slim-cut menswear sells in premium stores. Mid-market brands carry two size runs per style to cover cycling. Resale keeps growing.

fitness.state: DEXA-plus-coaching chains keep adding sites. Medicare Advantage 'prescribed lifting' expands with retatrutide on Part D. Staff for older lifters remain the constraint. Bariatric-surgery centres convert to 'medical weight' clinics.

insurance.state: Employer weight-management coverage fell from 64% to 49%. Covering plans restrict it to diabetes, cardiac, OSA, MASH and CKD codes. Pharmacy trend moderated to ~+6% as unit prices fell. Kiosk-weight premium tiers persist at the remaining gated plans. Life insurers price untreated BMI. Medicare Part A absorbs the fracture and fall costs.

pharma.state: Volume up ~30%, net price down ~10%. Lilly leads on retatrutide and tirzepatide; Novo holds orals and the federal $99 contract; Amgen's MariTide holds the premium monthly slot. Litigation reserves enter earnings calls. Bariatric device makers shrink.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Income, more sharply than before. A trained, DEXA-verified body on retatrutide or MariTide with a coach reads as top third. The $299 retatrutide pen spreads thinness downward, but without a coach the result is thin and soft. A cycling middle (on in spring, off after a job change) reads as the squeezed middle third. A 'clinic thin' look from free oral semaglutide reads as programme, which carries its own stigma.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The middle third is now the least medicated and the most visibly cycling. Men 30–49 in Charlotte's trades and logistics jobs lost employer coverage in 2035, earn too much for the FQHC programme, and split between $229 portal pills and $25 Indian pens. Thinness is no longer scarce; muscle is the uniform.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Protein-first meals are the norm for users. Hosts plan for 'on', 'holiday' and 'quitting' guests. Sunday full-table dinners and potlucks persist as heritage. Weekend dose holidays bring back Saturday feasts in some households.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles list regimen and now 'holiday days'. 'Coached' reads as income and 'programme' as poverty. 'Unmedicated' remains niche. Partners negotiate shared holiday weekends.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Medicalised. The alcohol and nicotine endorsements recast appetite as 'craving', a general clinical target. The backlash coalition is steady in size and now joined by recovery-movement traditionalists who object to 'pharmacological sobriety'.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. The randomised AUD trial (~9% vs ~4% SHAPS elevation) made 'the grey' a measured effect at standard dose. About 11M Americans are on top-dose triple or dual regimens. At the observational 12% vs 5% gap that implies ~770k excess cases if causal. About 5.5M 'calm' subscribers and ≈4.4M nicotine/alcohol users are partly measured or unmeasured. Weekend 'holidays' are reported by roughly a third of oral users in a 2036 Pew-style survey. They are pharmacologically meaningful for Foundayo (half-life ~1–2 days) and mostly placebo for oral semaglutide (~1 week).
interior_life.framing: Side effect, first in clinic and now in public. 'The grey' is a talk-show segment, a sitcom running joke and a campaign line. Subscription brands still market 'calm' under FTC terms but add 'holiday-friendly' dosing guides.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Fewer employers fund 'focus' through lifestyle accounts after the retreat; about half of large white-collar employers still do. Sales and hospitality staff dose down before peaks. Warehouse 'metabolic tenure' is fading as coverage disappears. EAP alcohol referrals now routinely include a semaglutide prescription.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Holiday weekend' culture: festivals, clubs and Nashville showcases schedule around Saturday highs. Stand-up about 'the grey' is a staple. Critics still use 'grey era'. A recovery memoir genre titled around 'quitting without wanting' sells.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists routinely prescribe holiday weekends for couples. Complaints focus on partners who 'don't want anything anymore'. Couples where one partner quit drinking on the drug report the partner no longer 'enjoys' them.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The 2036 presidential campaign argues over the HRSA programme ('free pills for some, $229 for you'), the parked generic and mass-tort ads. The Safe Pens bill is still stalled. Some state legislators propose 'anhedonia disclosure' bills; none passed.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA is data-demanding. It approved survodutide for MASH, is reviewing the AUD sNDA with anhedonia monitoring, contests generic forfeiture in court, and has nine exporters on import alert. It brings no individual prosecutions and has no authentication law to enforce. FTC consent orders stand.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: New direct subsidy: the Community Metabolic Access Program (enacted Jul 2035 in a health extenders package) buys orals at $99/month and gives them free to ≈6.0M people via FQHCs, quitlines and SAMHSA programmes, at ≈$7.1B a year of a $7.5B appropriation. Part D's $199/$50 terms and the 31-state-plus-DC Medicaid match are unchanged. No mandate.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The CMS continuation standard is unchanged, and the HRSA programme adopts it with a ≥5% response or a documented quit/drink-reduction goal. Kiosk weights continue at the remaining gated employer plans. Indiana and Arkansas keep their 12-month rules.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still pushes drivers toward tirzepatide. Fleets keep visual-field checks. The Army allows accession on stable oral semaglutide since 2035, a contested change. VA prescribes for AUD under its own guideline.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Chinese API and Indian product supply the 11M-user US gray market. The glibenclamide cluster prompted a DEA–CBP parcel task force and a US–India joint statement, but no legal import channel. Section 232 tariffs remain. The federal $99 contract is sourced from Novo's US plants and is a political talking point.

events.event: Annual benefits surveys show the share of employers covering weight-management drugs falling from 64% to 49%. Three Fortune 100 firms restrict incretin coverage to diabetes, cardiac, sleep apnea and kidney codes, and about 3M workers lose weight-management coverage at open enrolment

Under a new HHS portal agreement, Novo and Lilly cut direct prices to $199–249 for injectables and $229 for the 50 mg pill, and list retatrutide 12 mg in a single-dose pen at $299. The same pen joins Part D at the $199 statutory rate. Bariatric surgery bookings fall a fifth by year-end

Counterfeit 'Wegovy pill' tablets laced with the diabetes drug glibenclamide cause about 1,900 ER visits for severe low blood sugar and 23 deaths in Texas, Arizona and New Mexico. DEA and CBP form a parcel task force

Congress passes the Community Metabolic Access Program in a health extenders package. HRSA buys oral semaglutide and Foundayo at $99 a month and gives them free through community health centres and state quitlines to adults at or below 200% of the poverty line, including in non-expansion states

ASAM and VA/DoD guidelines endorse semaglutide for alcohol use disorder, and the Public Health Service tobacco guideline names it as a cessation adjunct. The trial behind the alcohol guideline is also the first randomised study to show more loss of pleasure on the drug than on placebo (9% vs 4%), and 'the grey' becomes national news
With about 92,000 claims consolidated, the first GLP-1 bellwether jury awards a Pennsylvania woman $11.2M on gastroparesis failure-to-warn. Novo and Lilly appeal and book litigation reserves

open_tensions: The middle third is now the least covered. Employers retreated to diagnosis codes, the free programme stops at 200% FPL, and the gap is filled by $229 cash pills and $25 imports. Meanwhile the glibenclamide cluster has not moved the Safe Pens bill, and generic entry waits on a forfeiture ruling expected in 2037.
Mass-market retatrutide on Part D at $199 puts ~30% loss into the oldest, most bone-fragile population. The ≈22,000 excess hip fractures a year are billed to Part A, and no budget score counts them.
The AUD sNDA decision (2037) will require FDA to weigh the first randomised anhedonia signal against the indication's own mechanism. The same molecule is sold at low dose to 5.5M people as 'calm'.
The mass tort's next bellwethers, the NAION claims and the reserve disclosures press on manufacturers just as the federal $99 contract and portal cuts squeeze unit margins.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is on the US market; generic_us remains false.
The permanent Part D obesity benefit pays the $199/month negotiated rate with a $50 copay, eligibility BMI ≥30 or ≥27 with one comorbidity, and the counselling visit.
The CMS continuation standard, including the 90-day bone-pause code, is unchanged, and the same 31 states plus DC use it for the 90% Medicaid match.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149–150 a month cash through the federal direct-pricing portal (launched as TrumpRx) and manufacturer channels.
FTC consent orders still bar 'anxiety treatment' claims while permitting 'calm' and 'focus' marketing for subscription brands.

prose.headline: Free at the Clinic, $229 at the Portal, $25 by Mail: America's Three Prices for Thin
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2036 more than a third of American adults take an incretin drug, about a hundred million people. What divides them is no longer whether they take it. It is who pays, and what the payment leaves on the body.

The poor got a programme. In the summer of 2035 Congress added a line to a routine health extenders bill. Under it the federal government buys oral semaglutide and Lilly's small-molecule pill at ninety-nine dollars a month and gives them away at community health centres to adults near the poverty line, including in states that never expanded Medicaid. About six million people now get their pills this way, along with a labs panel and a weigh-in. State quitlines hand the same pills to smokers and vapers, because the federal tobacco guideline now names the drug as an aid to quitting. Medicare still pays its statutory $199 and charges its $50 copay. Since spring 2035 that buys Lilly's triple agonist too, the pen that takes off almost a third of body weight. Bariatric surgeons have noticed.

The middle lost its coverage. Employers spent two years watching their pharmacy bills, then retreated. Fewer than half still cover weight loss, and most of those restrict the drug to diabetes, heart or sleep-apnea codes. About three million workers lost coverage at one open enrolment. They earn too much for the clinic programme and too little to shrug at $229 a month for the pill on the federal portal, so many cycle. In Charlotte, men who install HVAC or drive regional freight buy Indian pens for twenty-five dollars and the 50 mg pill when they can afford it. They wear the result: thin one spring and soft the next. In SouthPark, a few miles away, the bodies that come out of coached retatrutide and an annual scan are lean and muscled. Thinness is everywhere now. Muscle is the uniform.

The mail kept coming. About eleven million Americans use imported or counterfeit product. In June 2035, pressed tablets sold as the Wegovy pill turned out to contain an old sulfonylurea. Nineteen hundred people reached emergency rooms with blood sugar near zero, and twenty-three died across the border states. A task force formed. The authentication bill did not move. Generic semaglutide is still not on American shelves, held up by a court fight over whether the first filer forfeited its exclusive right to launch.

The drug also became a treatment for wanting. Addiction medicine and the VA now endorse semaglutide for alcohol use disorder. The trial behind that endorsement was also the first randomised study to measure the thing people had been describing for years: about nine percent of participants lost pleasure in ordinary life, against four percent on placebo. The grey stopped being a rumour. It is a sitcom joke, a campaign line and a question sex therapists ask at intake. A third of pill users take weekends off. On Lilly's short-lived pill that does something. On Novo's week-long one it mostly doesn't, though people say it does. Spirits sales are in their ninth year of decline, and some neighbourhood taverns in Milwaukee close each month.

Lawyers arrived as well. The federal litigation over stomach paralysis, bowel obstruction, pancreatitis and now optic-nerve damage holds about ninety-two thousand claims. In March a Pennsylvania jury awarded the first plaintiff eleven million dollars. The companies appealed and set money aside, and daytime television now runs plaintiff ads between pharmacy ads.

The bone bill keeps growing quietly in a part of Medicare that does not pay for the drug, now about twenty-two thousand extra hip fractures a year. Everything works, at least on the surface. The cost shows up in the waist, the hip and the weekend.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Renee Okafor, 46, office manager at a dental practice in Matthews, North Carolina, wakes at six and takes the 50 mg pill with four ounces of water, then waits the thirty minutes before coffee. Ninety pills cost her $687 on the portal, which she paid in March after the practice's new plan stopped covering anything without a diabetes code. Her A1c is 5.9, which isn't diabetes.

Her husband Marcus is already in the truck. His pills come in a white pharmacy bag from the community clinic on Monroe Road, free, the quitline sticker on the side. He hasn't vaped since February. He also hasn't laughed at the radio since February, and she doesn't mention it.

At work the hygienist, Tasha, talks about her weekend off. "Friday night I skip, Saturday I'm a person." Renee skipped last Saturday. She ate a whole plate of her mother's jollof and felt something, but she can't tell whether it was the drug wearing off or just the rice.

At lunch a patient's son asks the front desk if they know where to get the Indian ones that aren't the bad batch. Renee says no, which is nearly true.

On the drive home a billboard on Independence Boulevard asks: STOMACH STILL NOT RIGHT? A phone number follows.

Dinner is chicken thighs weighed on the kitchen scale. Their daughter Ada, fourteen, eats two and asks if she'll have to take it when she's older. Marcus shrugs. Renee says maybe it'll be cheaper by then.

She sets out tomorrow's pill beside the water glass.
